conventions.convention: AC is the standing assumption; the definitions themselves are choice-free. Results propagate the AC, DC and countable-choice hypotheses of their suppliers.
The fundamental form is ω(v,w)=g(Jv,w); the positive tangent orientation is (v₁,Jv₁,…,vₙ,Jvₙ), and ω=Σeⱼ∧fⱼ with dV=ωⁿ/n!.
On cotangent vectors J acts by pullback, fⱼ=−Jeⱼ, and ζⱼ=eⱼ+ifⱼ has type (1,0) and squared norm 2. Accordingly ω=(i/2)Σζⱼ∧conjugate(ζⱼ).
The real Hodge star extends complex-linearly. The integral pairing is ∫α∧*conjugate(β), linear in its first variable and conjugate-linear in its second; Λ is the adjoint of L=ω∧.
On the exterior algebra H=[L,Λ] acts by k−n in degree k, ε(k)=(−1)^(k(k−1)/2), and the primitive-star formula uses i^(q−p).

A polarization is rational, nondegenerate and (−1)^k-symmetric, pairs complementary conjugate types, and makes Q(Cx,conjugate(y)) positive definite Hermitian, with C=i^(p−q). The Tate shift V(−r) shifts both indices by r and retains C and Q.
Complex dimension zero is allowed separately: compact spaces are finite discrete sets, positive-degree forms and all differential/Lefschetz operators vanish, and the degree-zero star is the identity.

Fundamental-class evaluation uses the smooth-orientation normalization in which a positively oriented affine simplex represents the positive local homology generator. The manifold is compact and boundaryless.
H^(p,q) consists exactly of classes admitting a d-closed smooth representative of type (p,q), independently of the Kähler metric. The Hodge filtration is decreasing by holomorphic degree.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. On a compact Kähler manifold every de Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative; H^k(X;C)=⊕_{p+q=k}H^(p,q)(X), with conjugation exchanging p and q. These metric-independent spaces identify with H^q(X,Ω_X^p); the holomorphic-degree filtration induces their Hodge filtration and its spectral sequence degenerates at E₁. Holomorphic pullback and cup product preserve type, giving functorial rational pure Hodge structures on H^k(X;Q).

Defines compact Kähler manifolds, their orientation and complex-valued form operators, including dimension zero, and rational pure Hodge structures, Weil operators, polarizations, rational sub-Hodge structures and Tate shifts.

Assume AC. On a compact Kähler manifold, [Λ,∂]=i∂̄*, [Λ,∂̄]=−i∂*, [∂̄*,L]=i∂ and [∂*,L]=−i∂̄. The mixed anticommutators vanish, Δ_d=2Δ_∂=2Δ_∂̄, and Δ_d commutes with L,Λ,∂,∂̄,* and preserves each bidegree.

For a compatible Hermitian exterior algebra of real dimension 2n with the stated form-side orientation, H=[L,Λ] acts by k−n, the Lefschetz relations and unique primitive decomposition hold, primitive strings satisfy the stated factorial contraction formula, and L^(n−k) is an isomorphism for k≤n. With W=exp(L)exp(−Λ)exp(L), Wα=ε(k)J*α; primitive type-(p,q) forms satisfy *u=ε(k)i^(q−p)L^(n−k)u/(n−k)!.

Assume AC. For a compact smooth manifold X, natural coefficient maps give H^k(X;Q)⊗_Q F≅H^k(X;F) for every characteristic-zero field F, finite-dimensional in each degree. For F=R,C these identify singular and de Rham cohomology. They preserve cup products and are natural for maps between such manifolds; no positivity structure is asserted for general F.

Assume AC. For a compact oriented smooth boundaryless m-manifold, with the stated smooth-orientation normalization, a real or complex top form α satisfies ⟨J_M[α],[M]⟩=∫_Mα. Consequently cup-product evaluation of de Rham classes of total degree m equals the integral of their closed representatives wedged together.

seams_checked.note: The Hodge theorem's F3 retains AC, compactness, boundarylessness, real dimension at least two, formal symmetry and scalar positive Laplace-type symbol. Step 1.2 verifies these for Δ_d before using the smooth kernel and Green inverse; dimension zero is handled separately.

The logarithmic theorem's F3 uses finite-dimensional pure Hodge cohomology, functorial type preservation and E₁ degeneration only on smooth projective strata with supplied compact Kähler analytifications. The holomorphic de Rham interpretation is supported by the Dolbeault resolutions constructed in the compact theorem's step 3.2.

The Gauss–Manin construction's F6 faithfully quotes harmonic representatives, conjugation, metric independence and holomorphic functoriality. Its step 4.1 supplies the family-continuity argument separately; the compact theorem is not cited as already proving relative or monodromy semisimplicity.

The proper weights theorem's F4 and step 1.1 apply pure weight-q cohomology and Hodge–de Rham degeneration to smooth projective hypercover components. Mixed weights and singular descent are obtained from separate suppliers, rather than attributed to the compact Kähler theorem.

The downstream Lefschetz proof transports the supplied exterior relations using harmonic representatives and Laplacian commutation. The Hodge–Riemann proof retains ε(k), i^(q−p), complex-linear star and the fundamental-class normalization; rationality is conditional on a rational Kähler class.

The two-plane example uses Je=−f and Jf=e, obtains J(e+if)=i(e+if), and verifies *u=−iu and u∧*conjugate(u)=2e∧f. These agree with the primitive-star formula at n=k=1 and the norm-two coframe convention.
